<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

The **compute-function** half: a static config → the pure `@evoxc.defn` forward.

This module owns everything that describes *what the graph computes* and nothing
about *where it runs*:

* `forward_fn` — the `@evoxc.defn` forward `(params, input_ids) ->
  logits` for one static specialisation `(family, config, seq_len,
  batch_size, pack_weights)`, memoised so `id(fwd)` is stable (that is what
  makes two identical `evoxc_hf.build` calls return the *identical*
  `Executable`);
* `param_specs` — the `TensorSpec` of every graph input (the canonical
  per-weight tree, or the packed bundle);
* `reference_logits` — the independent pure-numpy oracle;
* `resolve_seq_len` — the single `seq_len=None` default.

The separation is deliberate and mirrors evoxc's value model: a config (plus
`seq_len`/`batch_size`) is a **static specialisation value**, so it pins one
graph; the params are ordinary **graph inputs** (`param_specs`) validated
at the run boundary and never `evoxc.constant` payloads. A forward therefore
captures no parameters at all — it is pure in its specialisation, which is what
lets `evoxc_hf.pipeline` cache compiled artifacts per specialisation while
weights change freely between runs.

Each forward returned by `forward_fn` carries its specialisation on the
object itself (`fwd._evoxc_hf_specialisation` — the plain-dict attribute
`"_evoxc_hf_specialisation"`), so `evoxc_hf.build` can derive
`seq_len`/`batch_size`/`pack_weights` from the forward instead of the
caller having to repeat them, and can reject an explicit value that disagrees
with the graph it was handed.

Import-time constraint: `numpy`, `evoxc` and sibling `evoxc_hf` modules only.
No torch / transformers / safetensors / iree at module scope.
